properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 1 at 2:25PM PST until November 1 at 6:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents.

* WHERE...San Francisco, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern
Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 PM PST this
evening. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from late tonight
through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.0 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) on
Sunday 11/01 at 3:59 PM. These predictions include up to 1.5
ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 1 at 1:36PM PST until November 2 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall will be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, including the following
areas, Hualapai Mountains, Lake Havasu and Fort Mohave, Lake Mead -
AZ side, Lake Mohave - AZ side, Northwest Deserts and Northwest
Plateau, southeast California, including the following area, San
Bernardino County-Upper Colorado River Valley, and Nevada,
including the following areas, Lake Mead - NV side, Lake Mohave -
NV side, Lincoln County and Northeast Clark County.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moderate to heavy rain is possible at times. Additional heavy
downpours may deposit between 0.25-0.75 inches of rain. With
saturated soils and significant run off expected, flash flooding
may occur.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 1 at 10:29AM PST until November 2 at 6:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated
surf expected. Minor tidal overflow during high tides.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Minor flood impacts are possible during high tides
with water flowing over normally dry sand and to lower parking
lots or paths. Moderate beach erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Additional flood impacts are likely into
next weekend with tides reaching 7 ft as early as Friday. Tides
will peak over the weekend into early next week 7.0-7.8 ft.
Elevated surf may increase flood impacts during this time,
especially across west to northwest facing beaches. Reminder,
tides mentioned have been corrected to reflect the most recent
trends in actual tide observations.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

NWSheadline: BEACH HAZARDS STATEMENT IN EFFECT THROUGH MONDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 1 at 10:01AM PST until November 2 at 6:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Onshore winds this afternoon with maximum wind gusts 20
to 25 mph, combined with elevated surf of 3-6 ft, and an
afternoon high tide near 6.5 ft will result in minor tidal
overflow.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor tidal overflow and dangerous rip currents.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will decrease Sunday evening, but
elevated surf will continue Monday with high tides close to 6
ft. High tide 11/1 will occur around 2 PM and high tide 11/2
will occur around 3:30 PM. Tides are expected to increase for
the end of the week, with tides reaching 7 ft as early as
Friday. Tides will peak over the weekend into early next week
around 7.5 ft. Reminder, tides mentioned have been corrected to
reflect the current trends in actual tide observations.
properties.instruction: Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Northern Coastal Humboldt; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 31 at 10:07PM PDT until November 2 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Monday evening. .

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.
